description: Nationwide #EndSARS protests began on 8 October 2020 against brutality by the Special Anti-Robbery Squad, days after a widely distributed video showed SARS officers dragging two men from a hotel and shooting one outside.
energy_note: A video on a Saturday, and a country in the street by Thursday.

description: The Justice Doris Okuwobi-led judicial panel submitted a 309-page report finding at least 48 protesters shot dead, injured or assaulted at the Lekki Toll Gate on 20 October 2020, that soldiers of the 65 Battalion fired blank and live rounds at demonstrators, and that the conduct 'could, in context, be described as a massacre'. It found the Army worsened it by refusing to allow ambulances to reach victims.
energy_note: A judicial panel used the word massacre.

description: The army said its officers fired only blanks. On the first anniversary the Information Minister said the 'only massacre recorded was in the social media'. The Lagos state government's White Paper rejected the panel's finding on the number killed.
energy_note: A 309-page finding, and a minister saying it happened on Twitter.

description: Amnesty International investigated on the ground the following day and confirmed at least 12 peaceful protesters killed at Lekki and Alausa, from eyewitnesses, video and hospital records.

aspect: The effect on whether anyone protests again
description: The lesson available to a young Nigerian is that a peaceful mass movement produced a panel, a report, a denial and no prosecutions. Political participation is priced accordingly.
energy_note: It was investigated, established, and nothing followed.

description: The japa wave in HLT-002 is frequently dated by the people in it to October 2020 rather than to any economic figure.
energy_note: A lot of people decided to leave that week.
